title: Node.js Examples
description: Copy-ready Node.js 24 snippets: HTTP and static servers, command-line parsing, a JSON file store, stream filters, an Express REST API with error handling, fetch with retries, a node:sqlite store, HTTP tests, graceful shutdown and a Dockerfile.

examples.title: Hello HTTP server
examples.description: The smallest useful node:http server: one JSON route, a 404 for everything else and a startup message.

examples.title: Static file server
examples.description: Serves files from a public folder with node:http, maps extensions to content types, serves index.html for folders and blocks paths outside the root.

examples.title: Node.js: Print a message
examples.description: console.log prints a value in the terminal. Text goes inside quote marks. Save this as hello.js, then run node hello.js.

examples.title: JSON file store
examples.description: A tiny persistence module: load an array from a JSON file (empty when missing), save it with indentation, and use it to keep a visit counter across runs.
examples.output:
$ node visits.js
This program has run 1 time(s)
$ node visits.js
This program has run 2 time(s)

examples.title: Line filter for stdin
examples.description: A grep-like filter: reads standard input line by line with readline, prints lines containing the search term and reports the count on stderr. Works on files of any size.
examples.output:
$ node filter.js " 500 " < access.log
2026-11-15T09:00:15Z GET /api/books 500 41ms
2026-11-15T09:00:20Z DELETE /api/books/2 500 9ms
2 matching line(s)

examples.title: Express REST API
examples.description: A complete in-memory CRUD API for one resource with Express 5: list, get, create with validation, update, delete, a JSON 404 and an error handler.

examples.title: HttpError class and central error handler
examples.description: Throw errors with a status code from any route (sync or async) and let one error middleware turn them into JSON, hiding details for 5xx responses.

examples.title: fetch with timeout and retries
examples.description: A fetchJson helper that gives every request a deadline with AbortSignal.timeout and retries network errors, timeouts and 5xx responses with exponential backoff.

examples.title: SQLite todo store with node:sqlite
examples.description: A small data module: creates the table on first use, keeps prepared statements for insert, list, complete and delete, and converts the done column to a boolean.

examples.title: HTTP tests with node:test
examples.description: Starts a server on a random port, waits for the listening event, sends real requests with fetch and closes the server in an after hook.

examples.title: Graceful shutdown for an Express server
examples.description: Handles SIGTERM and SIGINT by closing the server, exiting when connections are drained and forcing an exit after ten seconds; includes a health endpoint and trust proxy for use behind nginx.
examples.output:
Listening on port 3000
SIGTERM received, draining connections

examples.title: Dockerfile for a Node 24 service
examples.description: A production image on node:24-slim: cached dependency layer, production-only install, unprivileged user, health check against /health and node started directly so signals reach it.
examples.code:
FROM node:24-slim
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

COPY . .
USER node
EXPOSE 3000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://localhost:3000/health').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"

CMD ["node", "server.js"]
